summary: Rename Django User.note to customer_note via adding column, backfilling, deploying new version with a bidirectional sync trigger to maintain consistency during concurrent traffic, retiring old version, and dropping old column, while keeping the GraphQL public field name note.
write_consistency: A PostgreSQL bidirectional trigger automatically synchronizes note and customer_note on every UPDATE, ensuring both columns always reflect the most recent write from either version during the overlap period between deploy_new and retire_old.
revision_notes: Previous plans failed during deploy_new with 16 cross-version read/write inconsistencies because the one-time backfill only migrated pre-existing row data before deploy_new and did not reconcile ongoing concurrent writes from old version (writing to note) and new version (writing to customer_note) during mixed-version traffic. This left 15+ disagreeing rows and 7-8 mismatched/missing entries per column, causing read assertions to observe seed data, nulls, or stale values. This revision adds a bidirectional sync trigger during the expand stage that propagates writes between columns, guaranteeing that reads from either version see the most recently written value.

stages.description: Add customer_note column and create bidirectional sync trigger.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN IF NEW.note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.note THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; END IF; IF NEW.customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.customer_note THEN NEW.note := NEW.customer_note; END IF; RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER sync_note_customer_note AFTER UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note();

stages.description: Copy values from note to customer_note for all rows.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE note IS NOT NULL;

stages.description: Deploy new version with state-only migration; new version expects column customer_note.
Retire old version; after this, old version no longer serves traffic against the database.
Drop the old note column after old version is retired.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
